title: The Markov Equation x² + y² + z² = 3xyz: Tree Classification of Solutions
problemStatement: Classify all positive integer solutions of the Markov equation x² + y² + z² = 3xyz. Show that every Markov triple can be reduced to the singular solution (1,1,1) by a finite sequence of coordinate transpositions and Vieta jumps z ↦ 3xy − z — i.e. every solution lies in the Markov tree rooted at (1,1,1).
significanceNote: The Markov tree is the classical foundation (Markov 1879, Frobenius) of Markov theory: its coordinates are the Markov numbers, which form the discrete part of the Lagrange spectrum below 3 and are the subject of the open Markov uniqueness conjecture. This is the first Markov-equation entry in the gallery and is fully verified (0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide).
knownResults: Markov (1879) and Frobenius: the positive solutions form a binary tree rooted at (1,1,1), generated by Vieta jumping.
Markov numbers govern the Lagrange spectrum below 3.
Markov uniqueness conjecture (open): each Markov number is the maximum of a unique triple.
currentState: COMPLETED. Fully verified axiom-free formalization (proofs/Proofs/MarkovEquation.lean, 237 lines, 17 theorems, 3 definitions). The classification theorem markov_classification proves every positive Markov triple is Reachable from (1,1,1) via the move relation (transpositions + Vieta jumps). Proof by strong induction on the coordinate sum, with the descent inequality markov_vieta_lt (3xy − z < z for a sorted triple with z ≥ 2) as the engine.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE (2026-06-21, researcher-8): axiom-free tree classification of the Markov equation. Built from scratch over ℤ: IsMarkov predicate; markov_vieta (Vieta jump preserves solutions, with positivity via z·z' = x²+y² > 0); markov_root_prod (z + z' = 3xy, z·z' = x²+y²); the descent inequality markov_vieta_lt proved through g(y) = (y−z)(y−z') = x² + y²(2−3x) ≤ 0 forcing z' ≤ y < z, then x²+y² = z·z' ≤ zy < z² ⟹ 3xy < 2z; Step/Reachable move relation; sort_reachable (≤ 3 transpositions to a sorted representative); markov_reachable_one (strong induction on the sum via Nat.strong_induction_on, Int.toNat_lt_toNat for the descent measure); markov_all_eq (uniqueness of the singular solution). 0 sorries, 0 axioms (#print axioms: only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound).
insights: Fixing two coordinates makes the Markov equation a monic quadratic t² − 3xy·t + (x²+y²) in the third; its roots z, z' = 3xy − z satisfy Vieta's relations, giving the Vieta jump as a solution-preserving involution.

The descent inequality reduces to g(y) = (y−z)(y−z') = x² + 2y² − 3xy² = x² + y²(2−3x) ≤ 0 for x ≥ 1; with y ≤ z this gives z' ≤ y, and z ≥ 2 forces the strict maximum y < z (a tie needs x² = z²(3x−2), impossible).
All descent moves go strictly downward in the coordinate sum, so the classification needs only a forward ReflTransGen chain — no symmetry of the move relation is required.
(t,t,t) is Markov iff t²(t−1) = 0 iff t = 1: the singular solution is the unique all-equal triple and the unique terminus of the descent.
mathlibGaps: Mathlib has no Markov-equation theory; the ternary descent and Vieta jump were built from scratch (Pell's Solution₁ handles only norm-+1 binary equations).
nextSteps: Formalize the Markov numbers (coordinates of triples) and the binary tree structure (each non-root triple has a unique parent of smaller sum).
State the Markov uniqueness conjecture as a Prop.
Quantitative count: triples with max coordinate ≤ N grow like (log N)².
